title: Prune unused results and find short multiples via integer hulls

add.label: Conditioned failure bound
add.name: Correct guess and extraction failure under the coupling
add.explain: Condition on the coupled randomness shared by the two message experiments.
add.proof:
For a fixing $C$ of the coins of the coupled run $\mathsf{R}_\$$ with no target query, the conditional probability of $b'=b\land\mathsf{Fail}$ is at most $1/2$ because the output bit is fixed independently of $b$.
For a fixing $C$ with a target query, the same conditional probability is at most $\big(1+\Pr[\mathsf{Fail}\mid C]\big)/2$ by the pointwise bound $\mathbf1_{b'=b\land\mathsf{Fail}}\le (1+\mathbf1_{\mathsf{Fail}})/2$.
Averaging the two bounds over the coupled coins and the uniform bit gives $\Pr[b'=b\land\mathsf{Fail}]\le 1/2+(f_0+f_1)/4$.

add.label: Guessing probability bounds
add.name: Pivot-column conditioning
add.statement: For a stack $\mathbf W$, let $A$ be the matrix obtained by stacking its cells vertically. Then $\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)\le g^{-\operatorname{rank}\mathbf W}$. For every $v$ in its row space, $\operatorname{gp}(v^\top)\ge\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)$.
add.explain: Condition on the nonpivot coordinates of the independent input to the sampler.
add.proof:
Choose a basis of columns indexed by $J$, including column $0$ whenever it is nonzero.
Condition on $r_i$ for $i\in[N]\setminus J$, which fixes the contribution of all columns outside $J$ because column $0$ is zero if excluded.
The independence of the columns indexed by $J$ implies each fixed value of $Ar$ has at most one possible assignment to $r_J$.
The conditional probability of any specified $r_J$ is at most $g^{-|J|}$ by the sampler's independent choices on $[N]$ and its conditional uniformity at $0$.
Averaging gives $\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)\le g^{-|J|}$ since $|J|=\operatorname{rank}\mathbf W$.
For a row-space vector $v$, choose $a$ with $v^\top=a^\top A$.
For each $u$, event inclusion gives $\Pr[Ar=u]\le\Pr[v^\top r=a^\top u]$.
Taking maxima gives $\operatorname{gp}(v^\top)\ge\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)$.

add.label: Ledger interpolation bound
add.name: Security ledger by the quadratic chord gap
add.statement: Under (P5), for every integer $0\le Q<2^\lambda$, $E(2Q+2)\le (Q+1)/2^\lambda$. Write $U=2^\lambda-1$ and $F(x)=E(2x+2)-(x+1)/2^\lambda$.
add.explain: Compute the exact difference between the chord and the quadratic.
add.proof:
The first inequality in (P5) gives $F(0)\le 0$.
Adding the two inequalities in (P5) gives $F(U)\le 0$.
For $0\le t\le1$, expansion gives $F(tU)=(1-t)F(0)+tF(U)-(2\theta+20\varepsilon_f)t(1-t)U^2$.
Bounding the three displayed summands by zero gives $F(Q)\le0$ for $Q\in[0,U]$.

add.label: Charged mark bound
add.name: Charged comparisons from symbolic entries
add.statement: With $u=2Q+2$ in the extraction experiment, the probability of a charged first mark is at most $N_{\mathrm{cmp}}(u)(\theta+\varepsilon_f)+(\binom{L+3u}{2}+L+3u)\varepsilon_f$. Every run reaching its target query has a first mark of type $\mathsf{init}$, $\mathsf{guess}$, charged, or good. Write $\varpi=\Omega_{22}\zeta\zeta'\zeta''\varepsilon$ and $d_f=3D+2n+2K_1+6$.
add.explain: Classify comparison coefficients by their guess-variable degree before applying the grid bound.
add.proof:
Use the coupled run $\mathsf R_\$$ to determine the first mark by the coupling definition.
The symbolic game and the real run agree through the history before the first evaluated collision by the lazy-sampling demand.
No first mark is set before any collision or target query by (M1)–(M4).
A collision of formally unequal received expressions gives $\mathsf{init}$ by (M1).
A good collision cannot have a fresh guessed operand as the later entry, because its uncanceled fresh variable would violate the definition of good.
The later entry of a good noninitial collision is therefore a result.
If a good noninitial collision precedes a target query, (M3) sets a good $\mathsf{diff}$ mark.
If a target query comes first, (M4) sets a guess mark when its label has no entry.
If the label has an entry, the agreeing tables identify that entry as a symbolic key value.
In that case a good key value gives a good $\mathsf{key}$ mark by (M4).
Thus every charged first mark is accounted for by a bad collision or a bad key value in the evaluated symbolic game.
The monitor definition classifies all first marks as $\mathsf{init}$, $\mathsf{guess}$, charged or good.
By (M4), a run reaching the target query has a first mark.

In a fixed symbolic transcript, compare two specified entries or one specified entry with the key.
If the comparison contains guesses, choose a nonconstant guess monomial with formally nonzero coefficient.
The expression rules make this coefficient a nonzero scalar or a formally nonzero source-group expression.
At each fixed $r$, clause (e) of the incoming view result and $\varepsilon_f<1$ imply that the latter coefficient is nonzero on some valid encryption coins.
As $\varpi$ never vanishes on valid coins, the cleared comparison is a nonzero polynomial at fixed $r$.
The cleared guess-free term has degree at most $d_f$ by the incoming degree bound.
The cleared coefficients of linear guesses have degree at most $d_f$ because they are cleared constants or source-group values.
A pairing's product of two linear source expressions makes the coefficient of any quadratic guess monomial a field constant.
After clearing, such a coefficient has degree at most five because $\varpi$ has five linear factors.
The total degree bound is therefore $\max(d_f,d_f+1,7)=d_f+1$.
The grid polynomial bound with uniform guess values and valid encryption coins gives coincidence probability at most $(d_f+1)/(q-D)$.
This is at most $\varepsilon_f$ by its definition.

For a comparison with no guess variable in a source group, the incoming coincidence bound gives probability at most $\varepsilon_f$.
For one in $\mathbb G_T$, the incoming bound gives the same probability over encryption coins at any $r$ where the asserted equality is not an identity.
A comparison of distinct symbolic entries is nonformal by the symbolic game's entry rule.
A key comparison to $\kappa$ is nonformal by the incoming bound.
For an identity to give a bad event, the mark stack must be light because it is nonzero by the incoming demand.
All such $r$ lie in a single fiber of that stack by the incoming identity-locus demand.
This fiber has probability at most $\theta$ by lightness.
The total probability of a bad event for a comparison without guesses is therefore at most $\theta+\varepsilon_f$.

There are at most $L+3Q$ entries because each call has at most two operands and one result.
This bounds the number of comparison pairs and key tests involving guesses by $\binom{L+3u}{2}+L+3u$ since $Q\le u$.
For a collision without guesses at call $j$, the later entry is a result since a fresh guess could not cancel.
Its earlier partner is one of at most $L+3j-1$ entries.
A key test without guesses involves one of the at most $Q$ results or the two received target-group elements.
Summing the result-pair and key-test counts gives at most $QL+3Q(Q+1)/2+2$ non-guess comparisons that can account for a charged first mark.
This count is at most $N_{\mathrm{cmp}}(u)$ by substitution of $u=2Q+2$.
The union bound using these two comparison counts yields the claimed charged-mark probability.

add.label: Fixed-dimensional integer hull
add.name: Computing integer hulls in fixed dimension
add.statement: For a rational polytope given by inequalities in fixed dimension, the vertices of its integer hull can be enumerated in polynomial time in the binary encoding of the inequalities.
add.explain: Use the fixed-dimension vertex enumeration algorithm stated in the introduction.

ref.citation: R. Hildebrand, T. Oertel and R. Weismantel, Note on the complexity of the mixed-integer hull of a polyhedron, Operations Research Letters 43(3), 279–282 (2015), doi:10.1016/j.orl.2015.03.002
ref.locator: Section 1, first paragraph (p. 1) and vertex-description discussion in the proof of Theorem 5 (p. 4), arXiv:1412.2520v2
ref.quote: Hartman [8] gave a polynomial time algorithm in fixed-dimension to enumerate the vertices of the integer hull of a polyhedron.

add.label: Lift by integer hulls
add.name: Deterministic search for a short multiple
add.statement: Let $2\beta<q$ and $24\beta^4<q^3$. Given a nonzero $v\in\mathbb F_q^{N+1}$ with $v_0=0$, there is a deterministic lifting algorithm returning a short multiple when one exists and $\bot$ otherwise, in time polynomial in $N$ and $\log q$. In the ordering that deletes coordinate zero and moves the first nonzero index to the front, write $L_i=\{x\in\mathbb Z^i:x_j\equiv x_1 v_j/v_1\pmod q\text{ for }j\le i\}$. Call vectors bounded if their infinity norm is at most $\beta$.
add.explain: Find a bounded basis for each prefix span by enumerating the vertices of an integer hull in dimension at most four.
add.proof:
The nonzero bounded points of $L_N$ give exactly the short multiples after restoring coordinate zero, since $\beta<q$.
Every four-row minor of a matrix with four columns from $L_i$ is divisible by $q^3$ by integer column elimination on the rank-one reduction.
If the columns are bounded, each such minor has absolute value at most $24\beta^4<q^3$ by the determinant expansion.
Thus the bounded vectors of $L_i$ span a rational space $V_i$ of dimension at most three.
Start with the empty basis for the zero-length prefix.
A bounded point of $L_{i+1}$ belongs to $V_i\times\mathbb Q$ by restriction.
The lattice $L_{i+1}\cap(V_i\times\mathbb Q)$ has rank at most four by the dimension bound.
The lattice $L_{i+1}$ has a basis consisting of the least nonnegative integer lift of $(v_j/v_1)_{j\le i+1}$ with first entry one, together with $qe_j$ for $2\le j\le i+1$.
Compute its intersection lattice in these coordinates by taking the integer kernel of the rational equations for $V_i\times\mathbb Q$ with denominators cleared.
Compute a column Hermite form of $\binom{A}{I}$ with pivots ordered by row from top to bottom.
By unimodularity and independence of the nonzero upper columns, the lower parts of the zero-upper columns form an integer kernel basis.
Rational elimination and the Hermite bound give polynomial bit complexity in $N$ and $\log q$ because the two input bases have entries of magnitude at most $q$.
In the intersection lattice basis, the box cuts out a bounded rational polytope in at most four variables.
Enumerate the vertices of its integer hull by the incoming fixed-dimension theorem.
In the original prefix coordinates, the hull vertices are bounded lattice points that span every bounded lattice point by the convex hull definition.
Keep a maximal linearly independent subset of these vertices as the next $V_{i+1}$ basis.
After the $N$ extensions, return a basis point restored to the original coordinates if the basis is nonempty, and $\bot$ otherwise.
The $N$ polynomial-time extensions therefore have total time polynomial in $N$ and $\log q$.

edges.demand: For a nonidentically zero target-group comparison at fixed r, or a formally unequal source-group pair, coincidence over valid coins has probability at most ε_f. No expression equals κ formally. An identity in a nonformal target comparison prescribes one fiber of the nonzero mark stack.
After clearing by ϖ, a target expression minus χκ and a difference of source-group values are polynomials of total degree at most d_f.
A nonzero polynomial of degree at most d_f+1 in the independent valid coins and uniform guess variables vanishes with probability at most (d_f+1)/(q−D).
Lazy sampling of the label maps makes the symbolic and real histories agree up to the first evaluated collision.
The vertices of the integer hull of a bounded rational polytope given by inequalities can be enumerated in polynomial time in fixed dimension.
Hermite normal forms in polynomial time, with entries of polynomial size.

discharge.argument: The bound is the exact demanded inequality in the same experiment.
Rank at least four gives g^(−rank) ≤ g^(−4), below θ by (P3). The second inequality applies to the row-space kernel vector, and heaviness gives gp(W)>θ.
The statement gives the exact bound under (P5) throughout the required range.
The statement gives the exact charged-mark probability bound with u=2Q+2 and the required target coverage.
The algorithm gives a short multiple exactly when one exists.
The lifting time is polynomial in N and log q.
